transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I guess what brought me in is... I've been having some trouble with my eating lately. It usually happens after my evening class. I'm taking this advanced spreadsheet course at the community college—trying to keep my skills sharp for my bookkeeping job, you know? Everything is automated now, and if you don't keep up, they'll just hire some twenty-something who knows all the keyboard shortcuts. My boss actually made a joke about it the other day, which really got me thinking about my pension and how close I am to retirement, but still so far away. 

But anyway, after that class, I sometimes stop for food on the way back. The drive-thru is always packed with college kids at that hour, but I wait, and I end up eating a full fast-food meal right there. And then I'll grab candy from the vending machine in my apartment lobby, and by the time I get upstairs, I just keep eating more snacks. It's like I am making up for the whole day. But yeah, that software class is really taking a lot out of me.
Do you think you eat more after the class because you're feeling stressed or anxious about it?

I don't know if it's stress, exactly. I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean, the class is a lot, sure. The instructor, Mr. Henderson, he talks a mile a minute. He used to work in corporate finance over in the city, and he always wears these really loud ties. Just last week he had on this bright yellow one with little golf clubs all over it. 

It actually reminded me that I haven't been out to the driving range in years. My brother-in-law gave me a really nice set of irons for my 50th birthday, but then my sciatica flared up, and honestly, the fees at the public course have gotten ridiculous lately. It used to be ten bucks for a large bucket of balls, and now... well, everything is expensive now, isn't it? Even the fast food I'm buying on the way home costs twice what it did a few years ago. 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, anxious. I don't know, I don't really feel anxious when I'm in the drive-thru. I'm just sitting in my car waiting. It's a 2012 Civic, still runs like a top, though the heater core might be going because it takes forever to warm up on cold nights. But yeah, I couldn't really say if it's because I'm stressed about the spreadsheets. I just end up doing it.
Do you think you're eating more because you're feeling upset or emotional after the class?

Upset? I don't think so. I'm not sitting in the car crying or anything. My emotions are usually pretty level. My ex-wife used to say I was way too level, actually. She was the emotional one. She'd watch those evening dramas on the regular networks and just bawl her eyes out. Do they even make those shows anymore? Now everything is streaming. 

I tried to set up one of those smart TV sticks last weekend, and the passwords... you need a different password for every single app now. It has to have a capital letter, a number, a special character. I just write them all down in a little spiral notebook, which I know defeats the whole purpose of cybersecurity. My nephew told me to use a password manager app, but trusting the cloud with my bank logins? No thank you. I do bookkeeping for a living, and I've seen how easily numbers can just vanish or get messed up in a system if you aren't looking at a hard copy. You really have to keep a paper trail. 

But anyway, what were we saying? Emotional? No, I don't really feel sad or mad or anything like that when I'm getting the food. I just sort of... eat it all.
Do you feel like you have to eat when you're in the car after class, or is it something you choose to do?

Choose to do it? I mean, pulling into the drive-thru is a choice, I suppose. But later, once I get up to my apartment with all those snacks from the lobby... well, the vending machine down there is a complete rip-off, by the way. They just swapped out the old glass-front machine for one of those fancy touch-screen ones. It takes credit cards now, which I guess is fine, but they raised the price of the peanut butter cups by fifty cents. Fifty cents! And the packages are definitely smaller. I was actually doing the math on it the other day—occupational hazard, you know—and the price per ounce has gone up nearly thirty percent since 2019. It's robbery, plain and simple. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, right, if I have to eat. Well, once I actually start on those snacks in my apartment, it really doesn't feel like a choice anymore. I keep telling myself to just close the bag, put a chip clip on it, and go to bed. I have to be up by six for work, after all. But my hands just keep reaching for more and more. I can't seem to stop until it's all gone, and then I just sit there feeling totally embarrassed and sick of myself.
Do you feel like you're in control of how much you're eating when you're having these episodes after class?

Control? No, no I wouldn't say I'm in control. Like I was just saying, once I open those snacks in the apartment, it's like... I don't know, it's like a switch flips. I keep telling myself, "Just close the bag, put the chip clip on it, go to bed." You know, those chip clips with the magnet on the back? I bought a whole pack of them at the dollar store, but the magnets are so weak they just slide right down the front of the fridge. I ended up gluing little rare-earth magnets to them. You can get a pack of fifty online for practically nothing. They're incredibly strong, though you have to be careful not to pinch your fingers. My nephew was playing with them once and got a blood blister on his thumb. He cried for an hour. 

But anyway, where was I? Oh, the snacks. Yeah, I tell myself to stop, but my hands just keep reaching into the bag. It's like I'm watching someone else do it. I just keep going and going until every last crumb is gone, and then... I just sit there. I feel so embarrassed, you know? And just sick of myself for doing it again. So no, I don't feel in control at all.
Do you usually feel guilty after these eating episodes are over?

Guilty? Yeah... yeah, I do. It's like I was just saying, I sit there feeling totally embarrassed and sick of myself. It's a terrible feeling. You know, it's that same pit in your stomach you get when you realize you've made a huge mistake on a client's ledger. I had this one account a few years ago—a local hardware store, family-owned for three generations. The grandson took over and decided to digitize their entire inventory system over a long weekend. Absolute disaster. He didn't understand the difference between cash and accrual accounting, so he was logging unpaid invoices as received revenue. By the time I caught it at the end of the quarter, their tax liability looked astronomical. I had to spend three weeks untangling the mess, going line by line through hundreds of receipts. The grandfather was furious, threatening to fire me, even though it was the kid's fault. That's the thing about family businesses, they always circle the wagons. 

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, feeling guilty. Yeah, after I finish all that food, the guilt just washes over me. I know I shouldn't have done it, but it's already too late.
Does this loss of control while eating happen to you every time you're in this situation after class?

Every time? Well, no, not every single time. But it's been happening a lot lately. For about the past three months, I'd say there's usually at least one night a week after my evening class where I just lose it, eat everything in sight, and then... well, then I make myself throw it all up afterward. It's awful. Throwing up is the worst. It reminds me of this time I got food poisoning from a seafood buffet down in Florida. My sister insisted we go there for her husband's birthday. I told her, I said, "Martha, you don't eat discount oysters in August," but she wouldn't listen. She had this coupon she'd cut out of the Sunday paper—she's obsessed with coupons, has these little accordion folders categorized by aisle. Anyway, I spent two whole days curled up on the bathroom floor of that rented condo. The tile was this hideous avocado green, the kind you only see in houses built in the seventies. I must have counted every single grout line in that room. 

But, um, what was the question? Oh, right, if it happens every time. Yeah, like I said, not every time, but at least once a week for the last three months, I end up overeating and then making myself sick.
Do you feel like you're eating really fast during these episodes where you lose control?

Fast? Uh, I don't know if I'd say I'm eating really fast. I haven't really noticed the speed, to be honest. I'm just so focused on getting the food down. It's funny you mention speed, though, because I used to be a really fast eater when I was a kid. I had three older brothers, and if you didn't eat fast, you didn't get seconds. My oldest brother, Dave, he was practically a vacuum cleaner. He went on to join the Navy, actually. Spent four years on a submarine. I can't even imagine being cooped up in a metal tube underwater for months at a time. The smell alone must be terrible. He said they used to watch the same five movies over and over again until the VHS tapes wore out. Remember VHS tapes? I still have a whole box of them in my attic, mostly old recordings of the Super Bowl and some home movies. I really need to get those digitized before they degrade completely. There's this place downtown that does it, but they charge an arm and a leg. 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, if I eat fast during those times. Yeah, I'm not really sure. I don't think I'm rushing, it's just... I just can't stop once I start.
Do you think you're eating a large amount of food when you have these episodes where you lose control?

A large amount? Yeah, I guess you could say that. That's actually what brought me in, to be honest. After my evening class, I'll stop for food and just... I'll end up eating a full fast-food meal, like a double burger, large fries, the works. And then I'll hit the vending machine for candy, and then I get home and keep going with more snacks. It's like I'm trying to make up for not eating the whole day. 

Speaking of that evening class, it's a continuing education thing for advanced Excel functions. You wouldn't believe how much Excel has changed since I started bookkeeping. Back in the day, we did everything on green ledger paper. I used to have this special mechanical pencil, a Pentel 0.5 millimeter, that I guarded with my life. If anyone borrowed it and didn't give it back, there was hell to pay. I remember this one guy, Gary, he sat two desks down from me in my first job at this logistics firm. Gary was a chronic pen-stealer. He didn't even do it maliciously, he just absentmindedly put them in his pocket. One time, he walked out with my favorite red pen right before month-end close. I had to use a magenta marker for my adjustments. The controller thought I was losing my mind. Gary ended up moving to Arizona, opened a cactus nursery or something bizarre like that. I always wondered how a guy who couldn't keep track of office supplies managed a whole greenhouse. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the amount of food. Yeah, it's a lot. The fast food, the candy, the snacks at home... it's definitely a large amount all at once.
Do you think you're eating an amount of food that's more than most people would eat in a similar situation?

More than most people? Oh, definitely. I mean, nobody else in my class is eating a whole double burger, large fries, a couple of candy bars from the machine, and then going home to raid the pantry. It's like I have to eat a whole day's worth of food in one sitting. 

You know, I actually tried talking to my neighbor about it once, just kind of casually bringing up how much I eat sometimes. His name is Frank. Frank is a competitive eater, if you can believe that. He goes to those hot dog eating contests on the Fourth of July. He showed me a video once of him eating, I don't know, fifty hot dogs in ten minutes. It was the most disgusting thing I've ever seen. He dips the buns in water to make them slide down faster. Who does that? It ruins the integrity of the bun! I'm a firm believer that a good hot dog needs a sturdy, toasted bun. There used to be this hot dog cart outside my office building back in the nineties, run by this guy named Sal. Sal made the best chili dogs. He had this secret spice blend he wouldn't tell anyone about. I swear there was a hint of cinnamon in it. I tried recreating it at home once for a Super Bowl party, but it just wasn't the same. I ended up burning the bottom of the pot, and you know how hard it is to get scorched chili out of stainless steel. I had to soak it for three days in baking soda and vinegar. It was a whole science experiment on my kitchen counter.

But, um, yeah, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, if it's more than normal people eat. Yeah, it's definitely way more than what a normal person would eat after a class. It's just so much food all at once.
Do you make yourself throw up after every episode of overeating?

Every episode? No, not every time. But... a few times, yeah. After those late-night eating spells, I've gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just get so scared that all that food is going to show on me, you know? Like I'll wake up the next morning and my pants won't zip. 

I actually had to buy a whole new wardrobe a few years ago because my weight fluctuated so much. I went to this big and tall store out on Route 9, the one next to the old drive-in theater? Man, I miss drive-ins. We used to load up the station wagon when I was a kid and go see double features. My dad had this 1972 Ford Country Squire with the fake wood paneling on the side. It was a boat of a car, but it had those rear-facing seats in the very back, the "way-back" we called it. My brothers and I would fight over who got to sit back there and make faces at the cars behind us. One time, my brother Dave—the one who went into the Navy—he stuck his tongue out at this guy in a convertible, and the guy actually followed us all the way to the grocery store to yell at my dad. My dad was furious. He grounded Dave for a month, made him mow the lawn every Saturday at 7 AM. And our lawn was huge, almost two acres. We had this old John Deere riding mower that was always breaking down. The carburetor was constantly getting clogged. I spent half my childhood smelling like gasoline and cut grass. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, throwing up. Yeah, not every time. Just a few times, because I panic about the weight.
How often do you make yourself throw up after one of these overeating episodes?

How often? Well, if I really think about it, for about the past three months, it's usually been at least one night every week after that Excel class. I come home, do the whole eating thing, and then go straight to the bathroom. I always make sure to run the faucet so my neighbors don't hear anything, because the walls are paper thin. Plus, the plumbing in my building is ancient, you know? The pipes make this awful clanking noise if you turn the hot water off too fast. It's called water hammer, I think. 

My brother-in-law, Rick, he's a plumber out in Nassau County. He's always complaining about the crazy things people put down their drains. He told me once he had to snake a drain at this fancy restaurant and pulled out a solid silver soup spoon. Just wedged right in the pipe! Who drops a silver spoon down a drain and doesn't tell anybody? Rick kept it, actually. He polished it up and uses it to stir his coffee every morning. He's a bit of a weird guy, Rick. He married my sister Brenda back in '98, and at their wedding reception at the VFW hall, he insisted on having a live polka band instead of a DJ. Nobody knew how to polka except my Uncle Stan, and Stan had two knee replacements so he couldn't really move anyway. He just stood by the buffet table swaying to the accordion and eating cocktail meatballs. 

Uh, wait, I'm sorry, I totally lost my train of thought. What were you asking me? Oh, right, how often I do it. Yeah, so like I said, for the last three months, it's been about once a week. Usually that night after my class, I just overeat like that and then... yeah, make myself throw up afterward.
Do you feel a strong urge to restrict your food intake or compensate for the calories you consumed during these episodes in other ways, such as excessive exercise?

Excessive exercise? No, no, I don't really do that. I mean, I'm on my feet sometimes at the office, but mostly I'm just sitting at my desk looking at spreadsheets. Exercise isn't really my thing. I did buy one of those stationary bikes once, back when they were selling them on QVC late at night. You know those infomercials where everyone looks so happy sweating in their living rooms? I bought one, put it right in front of the TV. I figured I'd pedal while watching Jeopardy. I love Jeopardy, I've watched it every night since Alex Trebek started. I was devastated when he passed away. I actually sent a sympathy card to the studio, if you can believe it. I don't know if they ever read it, but I felt like I had to do something. He was like a fixture in my living room, you know? Every night at 7:30, there he was. My mother used to love him too. She always said he had such good posture. She was a stickler for posture, my mother. If she caught me slouching at the dinner table, she'd poke me right between the shoulder blades with the handle of her butter knife. 

But, uh, what was I saying? Oh, right, the bike. Yeah, it just ended up becoming a very expensive coat rack. I threw a couple of jackets over the handlebars and never really used it. So no, I don't exercise like that, and I don't really try to starve myself the next day or anything. I just... try to get through the day, I guess.
Do you feel like you're eating really quickly when you're having these episodes of overeating after class?

Eating quickly? I guess I do. It just sort of happens, you know? I'm standing there in the kitchen, usually right in front of the open fridge, and I'm just putting food in my mouth as fast as I can. It's almost like I'm not even tasting it after a while. I just want it gone. It reminds me of how my dog Buster used to eat. 

Buster was this golden retriever mix we had when I first moved into my own place. Sweetest dog in the world, but man, he ate like he'd never seen food before. You'd put his bowl down, and whoosh, it was empty in three seconds flat. I had to buy him one of those special bowls, the ones with the little plastic pillars in the middle? It's supposed to slow them down so they don't get bloat. My vet warned me about bloat. Dr. Henderson, his name was. Really nice guy, always wore these bright, obnoxious bow ties. He had one with little cartoon stethoscopes on it. He told me retrievers are prone to stomach issues if they eat too fast. Buster hated that bowl, though. He'd paw at it and whine, but it worked. He lived to be fourteen, which is pretty good for a big dog. We used to walk down by the reservoir every Sunday morning. The water there is so clear, especially in the fall when the leaves change. I took up amateur photography for a little while just to take pictures of those trees. Bought a nice Nikon camera at a pawn shop downtown. The guy who sold it to me tried to throw in a bunch of expired film, but I knew better. My buddy Steve worked at a camera store in the mall, the one that used to be next to the Orange Julius? Man, I haven't had an Orange Julius in thirty years. Do they even make those anymore? It was like a smoothie, but frothy. 

Wait, sorry. Eating fast. Yeah, I definitely do that. I just shovel it in really quickly until I feel like I'm going to burst.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you start during these episodes?

Unable to stop? Yeah, it really feels exactly like that. Once I start on those snacks, it's like a switch flips. I usually buy those giant family-size bags from the wholesale club, you know, the ones that are practically impossible to reseal once you tear them open? My buddy Dave, he works in payroll down the hall from me, he has this whole system for sealing bags. He bought this little heated plastic clamp thing off the internet. Dave is completely obsessed with buying gadgets online. The guy gets a package delivered to the office almost every single day. The mailroom guy, Carl, absolutely hates it. Carl's been working there since the late 80s, back when we did all the accounting on actual paper ledgers. I used to do the ledgers by hand too, right out of high school. My handwriting was impeccable back then. Now, with all the typing and data entry, my penmanship is completely shot. I tried to write a birthday card for my niece last month and it looked like chicken scratch. She just turned twelve, actually. They had a roller skating party for her. I hadn't been on roller skates since the 70s at this place called The Roller Roost... 

Wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Sorry, my mind just wanders. You asked about stopping. Right. So, like I was saying, once I start on those snacks, I keep telling myself in my head to just close the bag and go to bed. But my hands just keep reaching for more, over and over. I can't seem to make them stop until I just feel totally embarrassed and... I don't know, sick of myself.
Do you feel like you're unable to control what you're eating during these episodes?

Control what I'm eating? Yeah, I guess that's exactly what it is. Like I was just saying, once I start, I just can't seem to stop myself. I'll be sitting there, telling myself, "Okay, just close the bag, go to bed," but my hands just keep reaching in for more. It's like my brain and my hands aren't connected anymore. It's so frustrating. I remember reading this article once about how the brain controls motor functions. It was in one of those waiting room magazines, maybe National Geographic or Reader's Digest? I think it was Reader's Digest. My grandmother used to subscribe to that. She had stacks of them in her bathroom. She lived in this old Victorian house with this huge clawfoot tub. The tub was so deep you could practically swim in it. I always wanted a tub like that, but my apartment just has one of those standard fiberglass shower-tub combos. The caulk around the edge is starting to peel, actually. I need to go to Home Depot this weekend and get some of that silicone sealant. They have it in clear and white, and I can never decide which one looks better. The guy in the plumbing aisle last time told me clear is better for tile, but white is better for fiberglass. He had this little name tag that said "Hi, I'm Bob" and it was on upside down. I didn't have the heart to tell him. He seemed like he was having a rough day. 

Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the eating. Yeah, I just keep eating until I feel so embarrassed and just... sick of myself. I really don't have any control over it once it starts.
Do you think your lack of control over eating after class is because you're feeling anxious about something at that moment?

Anxious? I don't think so. I don't really feel nervous or worried right before it happens. I mean, the class I'm taking—it's just a continuing education thing at the community college for the new QuickBooks update—isn't stressful at all. The instructor, Mr. Gable, is actually incredibly boring. He wears these thick brown corduroy jackets with the leather patches on the elbows. I always wonder where people even buy those nowadays. It reminds me of my high school history teacher, Mr. Russo. Now *he* made me anxious, always doing pop quizzes on a Friday. Who gives a quiz on a Friday? 

We used to go to this diner after school on Fridays just to decompress, grab a plate of fries and put way too much ketchup on them. The diner had those little jukeboxes right at the table, you know the ones? You could put a quarter in and play three songs. I always played Bruce Springsteen. I actually saw him in concert back in '84. Poured rain the whole time, but nobody cared. My buddy Tom's car broke down on the way home, though. The alternator just completely gave out on the turnpike. We had to wait two hours for a tow truck in the pitch dark, and the guy driving it was eating a massive meatball sub the whole ride back. The cab of that truck smelled like garlic and diesel fuel for the entire forty-minute drive. I still can't eat meatballs to this day without thinking of that tow truck driver. 

Wait, sorry. You asked if I was anxious after class. No, I really don't think it's anxiety. I just walk in the door and head straight for the kitchen. I don't feel particularly stressed or panicked about anything when the eating starts.
How often do you make yourself throw up after eating?

Throw up? Well, let me think. It's been going on for a little while now. I'd say for about the past three months, it's usually at least one night a week. Almost always after that QuickBooks class, actually. I get home, I overeat like we were talking about, and then I just... make myself throw up. 

It's awful, really. The plumbing in my building is so old, I always worry I'm going to clog the pipes or something. The super, Hector, he's a nice guy but he takes forever to fix anything. Last winter, my radiator was clanking so loud it sounded like someone was hitting it with a wrench, and it took him three weeks to come up and bleed the valve. He said he was busy fixing a leak down in 2B. The woman in 2B, Mrs. Higgins, she has these two little yappy dogs that bark at absolutely everything. I think they're Pomeranians? Or maybe Papillons. They have those big ears that look like butterfly wings. I saw a documentary on PBS once about dog breeds and how they've changed over the last hundred years. It's crazy how much we've altered their genetics. Pugs used to have actual snouts, you know? Now they can barely breathe. It's kind of sad, really, what people will do just for a certain look. I had a golden retriever when I was a kid, Buster. Best dog in the world. He used to chase the mail truck down the street every single morning...

Oh, sorry. I'm rambling again. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about three months now, usually once a week after my class, that I overeat and then make myself sick.
Do you consistently feel guilty after these episodes of overeating and throwing up?

Guilty? I don't... I mean, I'm not really sure if guilty is the right word. I just feel kind of tired and gross, mostly. I haven't really sat down and analyzed if it's guilt, you know? It's just something that happens. 

It's kind of like when you buy something you don't really need, like this one time I bought this incredibly expensive espresso machine. It was one of those Italian ones with the shiny chrome and all the dials and pressure gauges. Looked like the dashboard of a vintage sports car. I saw it in the window of this kitchen supply store downtown. The store was next to this amazing little bakery that made the best almond croissants. I used to go there every Sunday morning. The owner, this French guy named Claude, he always had flour on his apron and he'd give me an extra croissant if I came in right before they closed. He moved back to Lyon a few years ago, though. Said the winters here were too brutal for his joints. I get that, actually. My left knee has been acting up every time it rains since I fell on the ice back in '98. I was carrying groceries and just went right down on the sidewalk. Smashed a whole dozen eggs. Had to go back to the store and buy more, and the cashier gave me this look like, "Weren't you just in here?" 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the guilt thing. Yeah, I don't really know if I feel guilty. I just haven't really thought about it like that. It's just kind of a messy routine at this point.
Do you feel like your eating habits after class are related to any emotional issues or stressors in your life?

Emotional issues? Stressors? I don't really think so. I mean, my life is pretty quiet these days. I go to work, I balance the books, I come home. There's not a whole lot of drama. I've been at the same firm for almost twenty years now. The office is right above this dry cleaner, and sometimes in the summer, when the air conditioning acts up, you can smell that chemical scent they use. It's not terrible, just kind of distinct. 

My boss, Mr. Henderson, he's a decent guy. A little cheap when it comes to office supplies, though. He buys these terrible pens that always skip when you're trying to write a check. I actually started bringing in my own pens. I like the gel ones, the blue ink. It just looks more professional, you know? I found this great stationery store two towns over that sells them in bulk. The guy who runs the place has this massive collection of vintage typewriters in the back room. He showed me an Underwood from the 1920s that still works perfectly. It makes this incredibly satisfying *clack-clack-clack* sound when you hit the keys. Nothing like the quiet little keyboards we use now. 

I remember when we first switched everything over to computers at work. It was a nightmare. Half the staff didn't know how to use a mouse. We had this IT guy, Kevin, who had to come in and give us a tutorial on how to double-click. He wore these bright red suspenders every single day. I always wondered if he owned multiple pairs or just washed the same ones every night. 

But anyway, no, I don't really feel like there's any big emotional stress or anything driving it. The eating just... happens when I get home from that class. I haven't really connected it to anything deep like that.

The diner had those little jukeboxes right at the table, you know the ones? You could put a quarter in and play three songs. I always played Bruce Springsteen. I actually saw him in concert back in '84. Poured rain the whole time, but nobody cared. My buddy Tom's car broke down on the way home, though. The alternator just completely gave out on the turnpike. We had to wait two hours for a tow truck in the pitch dark, and the guy driving it was eating a massive meatball sub the whole ride back. The cab of that truck smelled like garlic and diesel fuel for the entire forty-minute drive. I still can't eat meatballs to this day without thinking of that tow truck driver. 

Wait, sorry. You asked if I was anxious after class. No, I really don't think it's anxiety. I just walk in the door and head straight for the kitchen. I don't feel particularly stressed or panicked about anything when the eating starts.

doctor.intent: determine frequency of purging behavior
doctor.question: How often do you make yourself throw up after eating?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: For about the past three months, there has usually been at least one night each week after class when I overeat like that and then make myself throw up afterward.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of the compensatory behavior (throwing up after eating), which directly matches the manifestation of Additional Requirement 1.

patient.answer:
Throw up? Well, let me think. It's been going on for a little while now. I'd say for about the past three months, it's usually at least one night a week. Almost always after that QuickBooks class, actually. I get home, I overeat like we were talking about, and then I just... make myself throw up. 

It's awful, really. The plumbing in my building is so old, I always worry I'm going to clog the pipes or something. The super, Hector, he's a nice guy but he takes forever to fix anything. Last winter, my radiator was clanking so loud it sounded like someone was hitting it with a wrench, and it took him three weeks to come up and bleed the valve. He said he was busy fixing a leak down in 2B. The woman in 2B, Mrs. Higgins, she has these two little yappy dogs that bark at absolutely everything. I think they're Pomeranians? Or maybe Papillons. They have those big ears that look like butterfly wings. I saw a documentary on PBS once about dog breeds and how they've changed over the last hundred years. It's crazy how much we've altered their genetics. Pugs used to have actual snouts, you know? Now they can barely breathe. It's kind of sad, really, what people will do just for a certain look. I had a golden retriever when I was a kid, Buster. Best dog in the world. He used to chase the mail truck down the street every single morning...

Oh, sorry. I'm rambling again. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about three months now, usually once a week after my class, that I overeat and then make myself sick.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of binge eating followed by purging behavior, lack of control during eating episodes, and feelings of guilt afterwards support the consideration of both F50.8 (Other eating disorders) and F52.7 (Bulimia nervosa). However, the patient's behavior of making themselves throw up after overeating, which occurs at least once a week, more strongly aligns with the criteria for F52.7 (Bulimia nervosa). The diagnosis of F50.8 could still be considered if the patient's symptoms do not fully meet the criteria for bulimia nervosa, but the information provided leans more towards F52.7. Further questioning might help differentiate between these diagnoses, but based on the provided information, F52.7 seems more likely.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's behavior aligns more with Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (F50.8) or Other Specified Disorder of Sex (F52.7) by inquiring about the presence of guilt after the eating episodes
doctor.question: Do you consistently feel guilty after these episodes of overeating and throwing up?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt after the episodes, which aligns with a feature of Binge Eating Disorder (feeling disgusted, depressed, or very guilty afterward) but is not a specific criterion in the provided symptom profile for Bulimia Nervosa.

patient.answer:
Guilty? I don't... I mean, I'm not really sure if guilty is the right word. I just feel kind of tired and gross, mostly. I haven't really sat down and analyzed if it's guilt, you know? It's just something that happens. 

It's kind of like when you buy something you don't really need, like this one time I bought this incredibly expensive espresso machine. It was one of those Italian ones with the shiny chrome and all the dials and pressure gauges. Looked like the dashboard of a vintage sports car. I saw it in the window of this kitchen supply store downtown. The store was next to this amazing little bakery that made the best almond croissants. I used to go there every Sunday morning. The owner, this French guy named Claude, he always had flour on his apron and he'd give me an extra croissant if I came in right before they closed. He moved back to Lyon a few years ago, though. Said the winters here were too brutal for his joints. I get that, actually. My left knee has been acting up every time it rains since I fell on the ice back in '98. I was carrying groceries and just went right down on the sidewalk. Smashed a whole dozen eggs. Had to go back to the store and buy more, and the cashier gave me this look like, "Weren't you just in here?" 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the guilt thing. Yeah, I don't really know if I feel guilty. I just haven't really thought about it like that. It's just kind of a messy routine at this point.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's behavior aligns more with F50.8, Other eating disorders, or F52.7, which might not directly apply but could be considered in the context of the patient's loss of control and guilt after eating
doctor.question: Do you feel like your eating habits after class are related to any emotional issues or stressors in your life?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about emotional issues or stressors that might trigger the eating habits, which is not specifically covered by any of the symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Emotional issues? Stressors? I don't really think so. I mean, my life is pretty quiet these days. I go to work, I balance the books, I come home. There's not a whole lot of drama. I've been at the same firm for almost twenty years now. The office is right above this dry cleaner, and sometimes in the summer, when the air conditioning acts up, you can smell that chemical scent they use. It's not terrible, just kind of distinct. 

My boss, Mr. Henderson, he's a decent guy. A little cheap when it comes to office supplies, though. He buys these terrible pens that always skip when you're trying to write a check. I actually started bringing in my own pens. I like the gel ones, the blue ink. It just looks more professional, you know? I found this great stationery store two towns over that sells them in bulk. The guy who runs the place has this massive collection of vintage typewriters in the back room. He showed me an Underwood from the 1920s that still works perfectly. It makes this incredibly satisfying *clack-clack-clack* sound when you hit the keys. Nothing like the quiet little keyboards we use now. 

I remember when we first switched everything over to computers at work. It was a nightmare. Half the staff didn't know how to use a mouse. We had this IT guy, Kevin, who had to come in and give us a tutorial on how to double-click. He wore these bright red suspenders every single day. I always wondered if he owned multiple pairs or just washed the same ones every night. 

But anyway, no, I don't really feel like there's any big emotional stress or anything driving it. The eating just... happens when I get home from that class. I haven't really connected it to anything deep like that.
